title: Delhi High Court questions proportionality of Telegram ban
text: The Delhi High Court on Thursday pressed the government over its Telegram restriction, which we covered here, asking "how can we stop the rights of 150 million people just because one set of citizens are appearing in examinations?" Solicitor General Tushar Mehta defended the block on the platform's design, arguing that its message-editing feature lets a leaked paper be backdated to appear genuine, as he said happened in 2024, and that its bot-spawning, cloud-based architecture makes offenders near-impossible to trace. Telegram's counsel countered that editing a message does not alter its timestamp.
anchor: Delhi High Court questions proportionality of Telegram ban

title: Jio’s coming-out party
text:
Reliance’s Jio Platforms filed draft papers on Friday for Mumbai listing, targeting around INR 360 billion (USD 3.81 billion), which would be the largest initial public offering (IPO) in India's history. The raise covers about 2.9% of post-issue equity, valuing the business at around USD 131 billion.

Where the money goes: This is a fresh issue with no offer-for-sale, so every rupee flows to the company rather than cashing out early backers like Meta, Google, and the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority. The prospectus earmarks INR 275 billion (USD 2.92 billion) to repay debt at telecom arm Reliance Jio Infocomm.

The wider play: Jio Platforms has pushed beyond telecom into artificial intelligence (AI), cloud, and enterprise services, with an Nvidia partnership dating to 2023. Operating revenue hit USD 15.6 billion in the year to March 2026, with profit after tax of USD 3.19 billion. Subscriber numbers grew to 524.4 million even as headcount fell about 21% to 27,935.
sound_smarter: Jio's filing takes the record from the National Stock Exchange (NSE), which had claimed it only days earlier with a roughly INR 300 billion (USD 3.18 billion) offer-for-sale. The two make an awkward pair. NSE was existing foreign holders selling out; Jio is a fresh issue, but it routes the bulk of the raise straight to clearing Reliance Jio Infocomm's foreign-currency debt. Neither marquee float is the foreign-capital-attraction story a cooling market needs. Clearing that debt is what makes Jio's AI pitch credible, giving it room to fund 5G and data centres without leaning on the parent.
anchor: Reliance’s Jio Platforms filed draft papers on Friday

title: Vice Versa
text:
India's first-ever vice-president of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) has been appointed. The man of the hour, Vivek Aggarwal, is a former head of the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU-IND), India's central agency for tracking suspicious financial transactions, and currently serves as Secretary at the Ministry of Culture.

The new hat: The FATF is the Paris-based intergovernmental body that sets global standards on anti-money laundering (AML) and counter-terrorist financing (CTF). Aggarwal holds the role from July 2026 to June 2027, succeeding Giles Thomson of the UK, who moves up to the FATF presidency from 1 July 2026.

The runway: Aggarwal was serving as Additional Secretary in the Union Finance Ministry when India's 2024 FATF Mutual Evaluation was published. The 2024 assessment placed India in the "regular follow-up" category, the FATF's highest rating tier, shared by only four other G20 countries. This result set the credibility foundation for this appointment.

The brief: As vice-president, Aggarwal will support incoming UK president Giles Thomson, whose agenda is expected to focus on payment transparency and underground banking. India's direct contribution to that work is on digital payments, where United Payment Interface (UPI)’s scale gives New Delhi genuine standard-setting weight.
sound_smarter: FATF is the body that greylists countries whose AML/CTF frameworks fall short, with direct consequences for cross-border capital flows and correspondent banking. An Indian official at the leadership table gives New Delhi advance visibility into which jurisdictions are under scrutiny and a voice when the criteria for scrutiny are written. For a country that runs one of the world's largest remittance corridors and is aggressively internationalising UPI, Aggarwal’s appointment is solid operational leverage.
anchor: India's first-ever vice-president of the Financial Action Task

title: Modi lays foundation stone for coal-to-ammonium nitrate project
text: Prime Minister Narendra Modi laid the foundation stone on 20 June for a INR 250.16 billion (USD 2.65 billion) coal gasification project at Lakhanpur in Odisha's Jharsuguda district, India's first commercial-scale coal-to-ammonium nitrate facility. The plant will convert coal into synthesis gas to produce 2,000 tonnes of ammonium nitrate a day, using gasification technology developed by Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL). India imports chemical products worth roughly INR 2.7 trillion (USD 28.6 billion) a year, and the Centre has approved incentives of up to INR 460 billion (USD 4.87 billion) to promote coal and lignite gasification, targeting 25 projects and investment of INR 2.5 to 3 trillion (USD 26.5 to 31.8 billion).
anchor: Modi lays foundation stone for coal-to-ammonium nitrate project

title: Modi commissions three indigenously built warships in Kolkata
text: Prime Minister Narendra Modi commissioned three indigenously designed naval ships on 21 June at Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port in Kolkata. INS Dunagiri, the fifth Project 17A stealth frigate, carries BrahMos surface-to-surface missiles and a medium-range surface-to-air missile system. INS Sanshodhak is fitted with autonomous underwater vehicles for hydrographic and oceanographic work. INS Agray carries lightweight torpedoes and shallow-water sonar. All three were built in Kolkata by Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers (GRSE) to Indian Navy designs, with indigenous content above 75%.
anchor: Modi commissions three indigenously built warships in Kolkata

title: Breaking news, literally
text:
India became the world's top ship-recycling nation in 2025. The country has taken a 35.4% share of global tonnage, meeting a national target five years ahead of schedule.

By the numbers: India's share rose to 35.4% from 30.1% in 2024, with volumes up nearly 60% to 2.99 million gross tons, according to figures the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways attributes to the UN Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD). The leap clears the goal set under the Maritime India Vision 2030 to lead the world in ship recycling.

The Alang engine: The industry runs out of Alang in Gujarat, the cluster of yards that dismantles most of India's tonnage and feeds the domestic steel sector with scrap. The government plans to nearly double capacity toward 9 million light displacement tons a year through a master-planned expansion of the yard.

Policy scaffolding: A 2019 law aligned India with the Hong Kong International Convention on safe and environmentally sound ship recycling, which India ratified the same year. State support has run to USD 6.4 million to help 115 yards meet that standard, alongside a credit-note scheme that lets owners offset scrap value against new vessels built in Indian shipyards. India has surpassed long-time leader Bangladesh, where throughput has slid amid political turmoil and the rising cost of green-compliance upgrades.
sound_smarter: When the International Maritime Organisation published its first list of Hong Kong Convention-approved yards in 2025, Turkey and Bangladesh led it and not one Indian yard made the cut. India now scraps more steel than anyone, yet its pitch to European owners, who recycle under the EU's stricter regime, still rests on yards the global regulator has not yet certified. Tonnage made India number one; certification is what makes it bankable.
anchor: India became the world's top ship-recycling nation in

title: Advisers and dissuaders
text:
National Security Adviser Ajit Doval opened the two-day BRICS National Security Advisers' Meeting in New Delhi on Monday. The conclave drew Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi, Russian security chief Sergei Shoigu, and Iran's deputy security secretary Ghadir Nezamipour to one table.

On the table: Delegates are meeting under the theme "Non-traditional security challenges confronting the world today," covering emerging technologies, counter-terrorism, and security in the use of Information and Communication Technologies (ICTs). India is this year's chair of the now eleven-member bloc, which has expanded beyond its founding five to take in Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates.

The China leg: Wang attends at Doval's invitation, his second India visit in under a year, with a bilateral scheduled on the sidelines. The two last met in August 2025 for the 24th round of Special Representatives talks on the boundary question, part of a steady normalisation since the October 2024 patrolling deal that began winding down the standoff in eastern Ladakh. That thaw has since reopened direct flights, the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra, and Chinese exports of rare-earth magnets.

The bigger room: The meeting is one of a run of events on India's chairship calendar, with BRICS energy ministers due in Gurugram on 25 and 26 June, all building toward the leaders' summit India hosts in September. That summit will be the next time Modi, Xi Jinping, and Vladimir Putin share a table, after the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Tianjin last August.
sound_smarter: For Delhi, BRICS is one of the few rooms where it can keep Beijing and Moscow in steady working contact without owning the optics of a formal visit. Hosting the bloc this year lets India set September's agenda and draft first, and on a platform that moves only by consensus, first-mover advantage does count.
anchor: National Security Adviser Ajit Doval opened the two-day

title: 12 Indians among 13 killed in Qatar LNG blast
text: 12 Indian nationals were among 13 people killed and 66 injured in an explosion at Qatar's Ras Laffan liquefied natural gas (LNG) complex on Sunday. The Indian Embassy in Doha said Qatari authorities confirmed the 12 Indian deaths, with all injured in stable condition. The blast struck the Barzan gas facility as operations were being restarted; Qatar's Interior Ministry has attributed it to a technical malfunction.
anchor: 12 Indians among 13 killed in Qatar LNG blast

title: Six UBT Lok Sabha MPs defect to Shinde's Shiv Sena
text: Six of the nine Lok Sabha MPs in Uddhav Thackeray's Shiv Sena (UBT) formally joined the rival faction led by Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde in Mumbai on Monday. The six are Sanjay Dina Patil, Omprakash Raje Nimbalkar, Sanjay Jadhav, Sanjay Deshmukh, Nagesh Patil Ashtikar, and Bhausaheb Wakchaure. The number is not incidental: six of nine is the two-thirds threshold that shields the group from disqualification under India's anti-defection law, which otherwise unseats lawmakers who switch parties. The Thackeray camp has issued show-cause notices and signalled it will seek disqualification before the Lok Sabha Speaker, and failing that, the Supreme Court. The crossover is the second major rebellion against Thackeray since Shinde split the undivided Shiv Sena in 2022 and toppled his coalition government.
anchor: Six UBT Lok Sabha MPs defect to Shinde's Shiv Sena

title: Jaishankar begins Mongolia and South Korea visit
text: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar landed in Ulaanbaatar on Monday, opening a four-day visit to Mongolia and South Korea. He met Mongolian Foreign Minister Battsetseg Batmunkh, reviewing cooperation on mining, clean energy, and agri-processing. He travels to South Korea on 24 June, where he would hold talks with Foreign Minister Cho Hyun on semiconductors, critical minerals, artificial intelligence, and a review of the India-Korea Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), the bilateral trade pact both sides are reworking. The visit builds on South Korean President Lee Jae-myung's state visit to India in April, which set a 2026 to 2030 roadmap for the two countries' Special Strategic Partnership (we covered it here). Jaishankar will also deliver the keynote at the Jeju Forum for Peace and Prosperity on 25 June.
anchor: Jaishankar begins Mongolia and South Korea visit

title: Founder, founder, who's got the founder
text:
Meta will invest USD 900 million in Indian fintech CRED and make its founder, Kunal Shah, the global head of WhatsApp.

The terms: The investment gives Meta a roughly 20% minority stake and values CRED at USD 4.5 billion (INR 43,239 crore) post-money. The Series H round mixes primary capital with secondary share purchases, so only part of the sum reaches CRED's balance sheet. The company says Meta will not get access to its customer data, and the board has framed the round as a step towards an eventual initial public offering (IPO).

Who is Shah: Kunal Shah is a serial entrepreneur who built and sold FreeCharge, then launched CRED in 2018 to reward Indians for paying credit card bills on time. CRED now counts 17 million members, processes more than 40% of India's credit card bill payments, and posted its first profitable quarter this year. Shah steps down as chief executive but keeps his shareholding. Miten Sampat, strategy and finance head since 2020, takes over as interim CEO. At Meta, Shah replaces Will Cathcart, who led WhatsApp for seven years and now moves to a new Meta role building consumer products with artificial intelligence (AI) tools.

Why India: Meta counts close to 500 million users in India, its biggest market, yet WhatsApp Pay handled just 0.65% of Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions in May 2026, ranking ninth. The constraint used to be regulatory: the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) capped WhatsApp Pay at 100 million users to stop it swamping the system. That ceiling was lifted in late 2024, and WhatsApp Pay still went nowhere. Between them, PhonePe and Google Pay split nearly 80% of UPI, and a user with a working payments app has no reason to switch.

The real play: In March 2026, CRED secured final Reserve Bank of India (RBI) authorisation to operate as a payment aggregator, helping it onboard businesses and handle their settlements. Meta's plan for WhatsApp in India is chat commerce: small businesses selling inside the chat window, with payments built in. Winning the consumer wallet is a lost cause, so Meta is buying its way into the merchant layer instead, where CRED can process the sale even if the customer pays through someone else's app.
sound_smarter: Meta is buying expertise rather than a product. Shah's value is that he built loyalty and revenue among India's credit-active consumers without wrecking the experience, the exact problem Meta faces turning three billion WhatsApp chats into a payments and commerce engine. The clearest signal: an Indian fintech founder now runs the platform half a billion Indians use daily.

title: Byte out of Apple
text:
Tata Electronics confirmed a “cybersecurity incident” on Monday, after security researchers said ransomware group World Leaks had posted over 200,000 files on the dark web, purportedly including component design and specification documents belonging to Apple and Tesla.

The cache: More than 630 gigabytes of data, reportedly including emails, multi-year event logs, passport copies of employees, and proprietary manufacturing documents. One 52-page file carries Apple's proprietary markings on iPhone circuit board quality standards, 33 files reference Hosur, Tata's main iPhone assembly plant in Tamil Nadu. However, the authenticity and completeness of all leaked data could not be independently verified.

The response: Tata said its response protocols were deployed immediately and that operations remain unaffected. Apple was investigating the breach, with a source saying a "full analysis was going on." Tata had also received a ransom demand. Neither Apple nor Tesla publicly commented.
sound_smarter: Tata already builds roughly a third of India's iPhones and is Apple's most important manufacturing partner outside China. That scale is the bill arriving for India's manufacturing ambition: the faster Indian conglomerates absorb Apple and Tesla's supply chains, the more attractive they become to ransomware groups operating internationally. Cybersecurity investment has not kept pace with the contracts, and the country now wears that gap as much as the company does.
anchor: Tata Electronics confirmed a “cybersecurity incident” on Monday,

title: India auctions 10 more critical mineral blocks, expands exploration
text: The Ministry of Mines has auctioned 10 more critical and strategic mineral blocks under the Seventh Tranche, taking the running total to 56 blocks since the programme began, a clearance rate of 63% across the 88 blocks the Centre has offered. The tranche covered graphite, Rare Earth Elements (REE), vanadium, titanium, glauconite, and rock phosphate, and put blocks up for the first time in Gujarat, Uttarakhand, and Telangana. The Ministry also closed its Second Tranche of Exploration Licence (EL) auctions, lifting the cumulative EL total to 11 and extending the framework to Arunachal Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, and Odisha. The minerals feed clean energy, electric mobility, electronics, and defence manufacturing, the sectors India is trying to wean off imports under its National Critical Mineral Mission.
anchor: India auctions 10 more critical mineral blocks, expands exploration

title: RSVP, strategically
text:
Iran has invited Prime Minister Narendra Modi to the state funeral of former Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. President Masoud Pezeshkian's invitation was conveyed to the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) via a note verbale on Tuesday.

The ask: Khamenei’s funeral, delayed for months by the conflict, runs from 4 to 9 July. The body lies in state in Tehran before processions through Qom, Najaf, and Karbala, with the burial at Mashhad. Iranian sources say invitations have gone to several countries, with delegations expected from Russia, China, Pakistan, and others. India has not yet responded to the invite.

The precedent: New Delhi's last gesture on Khamenei's death was deliberately understated. Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri signed the condolence book at Iran's embassy on 5 March, the government's first message of sympathy, which we covered here. Sending a senior civil servant, rather than the external affairs minister or Modi himself, conveyed condolence while withholding political endorsement.

The benchmark: When Iranian President Ebrahim Raisi died in 2024, India declared a day of national mourning and sent the vice president to Tehran. The level of representation New Delhi now chooses will be read against both that bar and the restraint on display in March.
sound_smarter: India spent the conflict keeping every channel open, welcoming the US-Iran ceasefire memorandum while declining to condemn the strike that killed Khamenei. The funeral forces a visible choice that a condolence book did not. Whoever India sends, and whoever it pointedly does not, becomes a public marker of how far New Delhi will lean toward Tehran while Washington watches. The lower the rank, the louder the message.

title: Goyal to visit UK today
text: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal will visit London from 25 to 27 June ahead of the 15 July entry into force of the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) and the accompanying Double Contribution Convention (DCC). During the visit, Goyal will hold bilateral talks with UK Business and Trade Secretary Peter Kyle to review regulatory alignment, customs coordination, tariff liberalisation commitments, and the administrative arrangements required for implementing both agreements. The discussions will also cover the DCC's framework for eliminating dual social security contributions for eligible temporary workers and the operationalisation of market access commitments in key services sectors. Alongside the government meetings, Goyal will join business and investor engagements, including the India Global Forum, meetings with multinational companies, and an Asia House roundtable, as India and the UK work towards a bilateral trade target of USD 120 billion by 2030.
anchor: Goyal to visit UK today

title: Greer concludes visit to India
text: US Trade Representative Ambassador Jamieson Greer visited New Delhi from 22 to 24 June to lead bilateral trade negotiations with India, holding multiple rounds of talks with Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal. The discussions covered key elements of a prospective India-US Bilateral Trade Agreement (BTA), including market access, digital trade, supply chain resilience, and the reduction of non-tariff barriers, with both sides acknowledging significant progress by negotiating teams in recent months. The visit was framed as a step towards finalising an interim agreement, consistent with the joint statement of 7 February, that both sides cast as a milestone towards a comprehensive BTA delivering tangible benefits for businesses, farmers, workers, and consumers in both countries.
anchor: Greer concludes visit to India

title: India rebuffs Pakistan at UN and over water-war threat
text: At the United Nations (UN) on Tuesday, Permanent Representative Parvathaneni Harish accused Pakistan of politicising an Arria-formula meeting, an informal Security Council session, after Islamabad raised Jammu and Kashmir during talks it co-organised with China. Harish said a co-chair meant to be balanced had instead politicised the forum, and repeated that Kashmir is an internal matter closed to outside interference. India used the session to renew its call for Security Council reform and a review of outdated resolutions, the same decades-old resolutions Pakistan and China sought to spotlight. Separately, the Ministry of External Affairs dismissed a threat by Pakistani Foreign Minister Khawaja Asif, who said on 20 June that Pakistan would go to war if it judged its water security under threat. Spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal called the remark a desperate attempt to cover Pakistan's own failings.
anchor: India rebuffs Pakistan at UN and over water-war threat

title: RBI drafts AI risk rules for banks
text: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) wants banks to put their artificial intelligence (AI) under board-level control. Draft guidelines would require every lender to adopt a board-approved framework covering all models, with AI and machine learning explicitly in scope, and to assess model risk continuously at both the individual and enterprise level. Where risk runs too high, banks would tighten controls, restrict use, remediate, or decommission the model, and report to the board's risk committee. Third-party models would face independent validation, AI used in automated decisions would need human oversight, and generative AI that interacts with customers would carry extra cybersecurity controls. The RBI has invited feedback by 24 July.
anchor: RBI drafts AI risk rules for banks

title: Prime mover
text:
Amazon will lift its India investment to USD 48 billion through 2030. Chief executive Andy Jassy delivered the figure to Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday, a commitment the Centre called a record. The total folds in a fresh USD 13 billion unveiled the same day, stacked on the USD 35 billion Amazon pledged in December 2025.

The headline number: Of the USD 48 billion total, more than USD 21 billion is earmarked for artificial intelligence and cloud infrastructure, with the new tranche flowing to data centres across Mumbai and Hyderabad.

The tax pull: The timing tracks the Centre's Union Budget for 2026-27, which handed foreign cloud providers a 20-year tax holiday until 2047 on income earned by serving global clients through Indian data centres, plus a 15% safe-harbour margin on related-party deals, which we covered here.

The company it keeps: Amazon is not alone. Microsoft has pledged USD 17.5 billion and Google has committed USD 15 billion on comparable horizons. Amazon has now sunk roughly USD 40 billion into India since 2010, and is racing Walmart-backed Flipkart and Mukesh Ambani's JioMart for the retail market.
sound_smarter: Amazon is buying a 20-year tax runway, not just data-centre capacity. The Budget exemption only pays out on compute built onshore and sold to global clients from Indian soil, and it expires in 2047 regardless of when a provider starts, so every year Amazon delays is a year of tax-free cloud revenue it forfeits. Modi gets a record investment figure for the pitch deck; Amazon gets the cheapest large-scale compute in Asia.
anchor: Amazon will lift its India investment to USD

title: Petroleum Ministry rebuts claims against E20 fuel
text: The Indian government is again defending its E20 ethanol-blended petrol programme after a fresh wave of viral social media claims questioned its impact on engines, fuel quality, and insurance coverage. In a clarification issued this week, the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas rejected allegations that E20 causes widespread engine damage, attracts insects, or contains sugarcane juice, stressing that fuel-grade ethanol undergoes industrial processing and stringent quality checks before blending. On the insect claim specifically, Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) clarified that fuel-grade ethanol is distilled to eliminate residual sugars and contains insect-repellent denaturants, so nothing in E20 would draw ants to a fuel cap. The ministry also said industry stakeholders had found claims that E20 voids vehicle insurance to be incorrect. The intervention counters misinformation around a programme (we covered it here) that has become a cornerstone of India's push to cut crude oil imports, support domestic agriculture, and expand cleaner transport fuels.
anchor: Petroleum Ministry rebuts claims against E20 fuel

title: Heavy metal diplomacy
text:
India's Directorate General of Trade Remedies (DGTR) has opened an anti-dumping investigation into hot-rolled steel imports from China, Japan, and Russia, after domestic producers alleged the three countries were selling below fair market value and causing material injury.

Who complained: JSW Steel, JSW Vijaynagar Metallics, and Jindal Steel Odisha filed the petition. The DGTR found sufficient prima facie evidence of dumping margins above the minimum threshold to initiate a formal investigation covering import data from 2022 to 2025.

The product: Hot-rolled flat products of alloy or non-alloy steel, up to 25mm thick and 2,100mm wide, used across automotive, oil and gas, construction, and heavy engineering. Stainless steel is excluded.

The price gap: Chinese hot-rolled steel is currently USD 11 to 37 per tonne cheaper than domestic equivalents. China's finished steel exports to India more than doubled in April to around 232,000 tonnes, making it India's largest steel supplier.

Existing defences: India already has a three-year safeguard duty on steel imports running at 12%, imposed in April 2025 and tapering to 11% by its final year. Anti-dumping duties, if recommended by the DGTR, would stack on top and apply only to the three named countries.
sound_smarter: Delhi is treating trade remedies as a compartmentalised, rules-based process, separate from the diplomatic calendar. The bet is that all three capitals will accept that framing. For an investor audience, the signal matters: India's trade defence machinery will file where the dumping margins are, regardless of who is on the other end.
anchor: India's Directorate General of Trade Remedies (DGTR) has

title: The soft sell
text:
Prime Minister Modi arrived in Seychelles on Saturday as the guest of honour for the island nation's 50th independence day, his second visit after 2015. India signed eight agreements spanning digital payments, health, agriculture, shipping, space, capacity building, and extradition, and extended a line of credit worth USD 130 million.

The deliverables: India handed over a Fast Patrol Vessel named Lespwar ("Hope" in Creole), 10 utility vehicles, six ambulances, and five sailing boats. The civilian anchors are a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to roll out India's Unified Payments Interface (UPI) in Seychelles and an MoU on Jan Aushadhi, India's generic medicines programme. Modi also addressed the National Assembly, the first Indian prime minister to do so.

The backstory: India has tried to anchor itself in Seychelles before. A 2015 agreement to build military facilities on Assumption Island, renegotiated in 2018, was rejected by the opposition-controlled parliament over sovereignty concerns and reluctance to take sides in the India-China Indian Ocean contest.

The China backdrop: Beijing has been courting Seychelles since at least 2011, when China's defence minister visited with a 40-member delegation and Seychelles invited Chinese naval vessels to use the archipelago for resupply.
sound_smarter: The genius of today's package is that none of it requires a parliamentary vote. Digital payment infrastructure, affordable medicines, and skills centres do not look like foreign military presence. They look like friendship. But once Seychelles' merchants run on UPI, its clinics stock Indian generics, and its civil servants train at Indian-funded centres, the relationship is stickier than any 20-year base lease and far harder for an opposition parliament to cancel.
anchor: Prime Minister Modi arrived in Seychelles on Saturday

title: Rubio says Trump expected to visit India early next year
text: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio told the Indo-Asian News Service (IANS) that President Donald Trump is expected to visit India in early 2027, adding that he planned to travel to India later this year to prepare. Modi and Trump met on the sidelines of the G7 summit in France last week, with Trump calling the conversation "very good." On trade, Rubio said the two sides were "on the last inches" of concluding a bilateral deal. The visit would come after a difficult year in bilateral relations: Washington imposed high tariffs on Indian goods, engaged closely with Pakistan, and saw ties further strained by the killing of three Indian sailors in US Navy strikes on commercial ships in the Gulf.
anchor: Rubio says Trump expected to visit India early next year

title: Japan's Takaichi to visit New Delhi for annual summit
text: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi will visit New Delhi from 1 to 3 July for the 16th India-Japan Annual Summit, her first official visit to India since taking office. The summit follows Modi's trip to Tokyo in August 2025 for the 15th edition. Both sides are expected to review cooperation across the India-Japan Special Strategic and Global Partnership, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said.
anchor: Japan's Takaichi to visit New Delhi for annual summit

title: India sends military airlift with rescue team to earthquake-hit Venezuela
text: India dispatched two Indian Air Force (IAF) C-17 Globemaster aircraft to Venezuela on 26 June carrying 30 tonnes of relief supplies, six tonnes of medicines, and a 41-member rescue and medical team in response to a devastating earthquake. The mission, dubbed Operation Amistad, includes a field hospital unit and two BHISHM portable hospitals. India's Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) deployments have historically focused on the Indian Ocean neighbourhood; a military airlift to Latin America marks a notable extension of that reach.
anchor: India sends military airlift with rescue team to earthquake-hit Venezuela

title: Charge sheet
text:
The Delhi Cabinet approved a new electric vehicle (EV) policy worth INR 150 billion (USD 1.59 billion), banning registration of new internal combustion engine (ICE) three-wheelers and light commercial trucks from 1 January 2027.

The mandate: Only electric three-wheelers and N1-category trucks will be eligible for new registration in Delhi from January 2027. Two-wheelers follow from 1 April 2028. School buses must convert at least 10% of their fleet to electric within two years. Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said the policy takes effect on 1 July and runs until 31 March 2030.

The pollution case: Delhi regularly ranks among the world's most polluted capitals, with its Air Quality Index (AQI) hitting "severe" levels each winter. Transport Commissioner Niharika said 33% of the city's pollution comes from commercial goods vehicles and 46% from two-wheelers and three-wheelers. "The policy focuses on these vehicles specifically. We are trying to convert the entire fleet of these vehicles into EV," she said.

The money: Purchase subsidies for two-wheelers start at INR 30,000 and taper over three years. Three-wheelers get INR 50,000 (USD 530) in year one, N1 trucks INR 100,000 (USD 1,060). Scrapping incentives for vehicles meeting Bharat Stage IV (BS-IV) emission norms or below run up to INR 100,000 for four-wheeler owners switching to electric. There are no subsidies for hybrids. The city plans 32,000 charging points over four years, funded by the Centre's PM e-Drive scheme and Delhi's own budget.
sound_smarter: Delhi is the first Indian city to ban new ICE registrations in any vehicle category, and the policy targets the right slice: the vehicles its own officials say drive nearly 80% of vehicular pollution. For EV manufacturers and charging companies, a registration ban is a market guarantee that a subsidy never is. The caveat: the winter smog that lands Delhi on global front pages owes as much to crop stubble burning in Punjab and Haryana as to tailpipes. The EV ban addresses what Delhi can legislate. The crop fires that choke the capital every October are a Centre-state problem no city transport policy will fix.
anchor: The Delhi Cabinet approved a new electric vehicle

title: Scrappy negotiations
text:
India has formally requested an exemption from European Union (EU) metal scrap export restrictions, warning the curbs could raise costs and undermine the recently concluded trade pact before it takes effect.

The regulation: From May 2027, the EU's revised waste shipment regulation will bar exports of non-hazardous waste, including metal scrap, to non-OECD countries unless specific approvals are granted by November 2026. The European Commission is also weighing a separate measure to restrict aluminium scrap exports, with a decision delayed to September.

India's exposure: The world's second-largest crude steel producer imported around 366,000 tonnes of aluminium scrap from the EU in 2025 and was the bloc's largest buyer in the first quarter of 2026. The Engineering Export Promotion Council of India (EEPC) warned that EU curbs would tighten supply and push up input costs for domestic steelmakers.

The ask: India has formally applied to retain access to recyclable materials under the new regime. Export quotas, rather than an outright ban, are currently under discussion.

Narrowing alternatives: A United Arab Emirates (UAE) scrap export ban introduced in June compounds the pressure. India sources roughly a fifth of its scrap from Gulf states, and the Material Recycling Association of India has warned that growing resource nationalism across aluminium, copper, and other recycled metals could fuel procurement costs and intensify competition among importing nations.
sound_smarter: The India-EU Free Trade Agreement (FTA) was built around tariffs and goods access. The scrap dispute shows that Brussels' environmental regulatory machinery operates through instruments that sit entirely outside the negotiated text, and each one can redraw market access unilaterally. Even if India secures this exemption, the pattern is set: the terms of access to the EU market are increasingly written in environmental regulation, and India has no seat at that table.
anchor: India has formally requested an exemption from European

title: Centre lifts fuel restrictions from 1 July
text: The Centre has withdrawn temporary restrictions on petrol and diesel sales, effective 1 July. The measures, imposed on 12 June, had capped daily diesel purchases at 200 litres per customer at retail outlets and barred commercial buyers from retail pumps. The government held retail fuel prices steady during the West Asia crisis, opening a gap of roughly INR 40 (USD 0.42) per litre between retail and bulk diesel.
anchor: Centre lifts fuel restrictions from 1 July

title: India sends Governor, deputy minister to Khamenei funeral
text: Bihar Governor Syed Ata Hasnain and Minister of State for External Affairs Pabitra Margherita will represent India at the funeral of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in Iran. Earlier, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian had invited Prime Minister Modi to attend (we covered it here). The ceremonies run from 4 to 9 July, concluding with Khamenei's burial at the Imam Reza shrine in Mashhad.
anchor: India sends Governor, deputy minister to Khamenei funeral

title: Note
text: India’s Ministry of External Affairs is headed by the Minister of External Affairs S. Jaishankar, who is assisted by the Ministers of State for External Affairs, including Pabitra Margherita.
anchor: Note

title: Core breach
text:
The Tata Electronics files dumped on the dark web include supplier maps and component photos for Apple's unreleased iPhone 18 Pro, the most sensitive material yet found in a breach we covered when it first broke.

What is new: The breach includes at least six documents mapping the unreleased iPhone18 Pro parts to the specific firms that supply them, covering chips on the main circuit board, the battery, and the cameras. Several carried Apple confidential watermarks and internal code-names consistent with the iPhone 18 Pro generation. The folder also held photographs of handsets undergoing drop tests at a Tata plant, dated early 2026.

Why it matters more now: The first tranche, more than 200,000 files posted by ransomware group World Leaks, held design papers for iPhones already on the market. The new documents map a phone Apple has not yet launched, on track for a September release, and the iPhone is the company's single biggest source of revenue. Apple does not disclose in its public supplier database which firm makes which part, and the leaked files show both where it draws a component from several suppliers and where it relies on just one.
sound_smarter: Apple's secrecy works by compartmentalisation, and a named supplier map shows competitors where Apple holds bargaining power and where a single vendor is its weak point. It lands at the assembler India has made the centrepiece of its electronics push, at a time Tata is still proving it can guard Apple's secrets as tightly as Shenzhen did.
anchor: The Tata Electronics files dumped on the dark

title: Bond spree
text:
Foreign investors bought a record USD 3 billion of Indian government bonds in June after New Delhi scrapped key taxes to lure global capital.

The surge: This single-month inflow under the Fully Accessible Route (FAR) dwarfs the USD 1.7 billion net purchases seen over the entire January-May period. Purchases of treasury bills hit record levels too, with almost all the buying happening in June.

The catalyst: The central bank (RBI) rolled out dollar-attracting liquidity measures in early June, including exempting foreign portfolio investors from income and capital gains tax on government securities. The RBI also added longer-dated sovereign debt to the FAR channel (we covered it here).

Index inclusion: Market players note these changes dismantle operational friction, positioning India for entry into the Bloomberg Global Aggregate Bond Index. India is actively pushing for inclusion, which could unlock an estimated USD 20-25 billion in passive inflows. However, other operational friction, including cumbersome settlement and post-trade processes is holding back inclusion.

Macro tailwinds: A 20% plunge in Brent crude prices back to pre-Iran war levels has further sweetened the deal for Indian debt.
sound_smarter: Securing a steady base of institutional foreign capital helps finance India’s spending and stabilize the rupee. By reducing the need for market-distorting interventions by the RBI (like the ones we covered here and here), this steady capital flow ultimately boosts India’s credibility as a premier destination for global capital.
anchor: Foreign investors bought a record USD 3 billion

title: Betting on the right ship
text:
Adani Ports will sell a 49% stake in the company that operates Kerala's Vizhinjam Port to MSC Group for USD 1.4 billion, valuing the transhipment hub at USD 2.85 billion. It is the largest foreign private investment in Indian port infrastructure.

Who owns what: Vizhinjam is owned by the Government of Kerala through a state entity, Vizhinjam International Seaport Limited (VISL). Adani runs it under a 40-year build-operate-transfer concession held by its subsidiary, Adani Vizhinjam Port Private Limited (AVPPL). MSC is buying 49% of the concession company. This is Adani's third tie-up with MSC after joint ventures at Mundra and Ennore.

Where the money goes: MSC, the world's largest container shipping line, is investing through its terminal arm, Terminal Investment (TiL). The structure makes MSC both Vizhinjam's biggest prospective user and a part-owner, so the handling fees its ships generate by calling at the port now partly return to MSC rather than flowing entirely to the rival hubs it currently uses.

Why Vizhinjam: The port is India's only deep-water terminal sitting directly on the main east-west shipping lane, about 10 nautical miles off it, with an 18 to 20 metre natural draft that needs no dredging. That lets it take the mega-vessels most Indian ports cannot, the physical precondition for pulling mainline services away from Colombo, Singapore, and Jebel Ali, where roughly 75% of India's transhipment cargo is currently routed.

The Kerala gate: Under the concession agreement, any ownership change above 25% needs the Kerala government's approval, and as the asset's owner the state has a real say. Shashi Tharoor, the local Member of Parliament (MP), has welcomed the investment but is pressing for a national-security and critical-infrastructure review before it clears.
sound_smarter: India has wanted a transhipment hub for years, while its containers kept flowing through Colombo, Singapore, and Jebel Ali. Building the port was never the hard part; giving a global carrier a reason to use it was. A 49% stake gives MSC a direct financial incentive to use it as a transhipment hub.
anchor: Adani Ports will sell a 49% stake in

title: Centre extends petrochemical duty waiver to July 15
text: The Centre has extended its full customs duty exemption on critical petrochemical imports until July 15, 2026, a fortnight beyond the June 30 deadline it was due to expire. The waiver, introduced in April as a temporary measure after the West Asia conflict disrupted supply chains and Indian refiners were directed to prioritise liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) production, covers the same product list as before. The government states that the fifteen-day extension is meant to ease the transition as the situation normalises.
anchor: Centre extends petrochemical duty waiver to July 15

title: UPI goes live in Greece, its tenth overseas market
text: India's Unified Payments Interface (UPI) went live in Greece on June 30 through a partnership between Greece's Eurobank and NPCI's international arm, NIPL. The launch lets Indian travellers, students, and the diaspora pay Greek merchants and make transfers straight from their existing Indian bank accounts using the UPI apps they use at home. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal witnessed the launch in Athens during a delegation visit that included the India-Greece Business Forum and sectoral roundtables on infrastructure, digital innovation and defence, and food processing.
anchor: UPI goes live in Greece, its tenth overseas market

title: Rising sun, rising stakes
text:
On Thursday, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Japanese counterpart Sanae Takaichi signed India and Japan's first defence co-development agreement in New Delhi. The two leaders also adopted three landmark documents on economic security, energy resilience, and artificial intelligence. Takaichi is on a three-day official visit to attend the 16th India-Japan Annual Summit.

Defence first: The two governments reached agreement in principle on the remaining technical details of the Unified Complex Radio Antenna (UNICORN) project, an integrated ship mast for the Indian Navy that both sides have been co-developing. They also agreed to explore further defence equipment projects. India and Japan sit in the QUAD grouping with Australia and the United States, widely seen as a bloc formed to counter China's rising influence in the Indo-Pacific.

Money on the table: Bilateral trade reached USD 27.5 billion in the last financial year, and Modi's Tokyo visit last year secured a Japanese pledge to more than double investment in India to over USD 61 billion by the mid-2030s. Japan already backs the Mumbai-Ahmedabad high-speed rail corridor and recently took a 20% stake in Yes Bank, one of India’s largest private-sector lenders, for USD 1.6 billion.

The AI track: India and Japan elevated themselves to strategic partners on artificial intelligence (AI) research and development, spanning data centres, compute, and semiconductors. The two sides set a target of sending 500 skilled Indian AI professionals to Japan by 2030 and backed new tie-ups between Indian firms and Japanese counterparts, including a research pact on large language models (LLMs) between the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay and Japan's National Institute of Informatics.

The energy play: The two oil importers agreed to coordinate strategic petroleum stockpiles, share market information, and explore joint upstream investments in third countries, building what both sides call the voice of energy-consuming nations.
sound_smarter: In a volatile global economy, India and Japan have arrived at something rare: a partnership where every major deliverable addresses a vulnerability both actually share. Together they can move oil markets, pressure mineral suppliers, and build chip supply chains that neither could credibly threaten alone.

title: Handle with care
text:
India has asked WhatsApp to pause its planned username feature before it launches. On Wednesday, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeITY) directed Meta to explain within three days why regulatory action should not be taken and asked the company to hold off on rolling out the feature in India until consultations are complete.

The feature: The ministry said WhatsApp's planned usernames would allow users to start conversations without revealing their phone numbers, raising concerns about anonymous communication.

Meta's response: A Meta spokesperson confirmed the company has announced the option for users to reserve a preferred username, but said the feature is not yet live. Usernames have initially been reserved for public figures, government entities and verified Meta accounts to reduce impersonation risks.

Regulatory backdrop: The move follows India's recent court victory over Telegram's temporary ban (we covered it here). The government successfully argued that username-based interactions and hidden phone numbers created enforcement challenges
sound_smarter: India did not wait for evidence of misuse this time. The Telegram ruling gave regulators a playbook, where anonymity features can create enforcement gaps. New Delhi is now applying that logic pre-emptively, pushing to stop potentially problematic features before they reach users.

title: Winter is coming, so are the curbs
text:
The Delhi government announced a sweeping set of proactive pollution-reduction measures on Wednesday to combat its notorious winter air pollution months before the smog sets in.

The shift: Previously, authorities triggered restrictions only after air quality deteriorated. Now, curbs will run continuously from November 1 to February 28, regardless of the AQI.

The restrictions: Measures include doubling parking fees to disincentivize private vehicles, staggered government office hours, and a blanket ban on non-essential outdoor civil construction.

Work from home: Between November 1 and January 31, both public and private offices must transition 50% of their staff to remote work. Violators face prosecution.

Sweetening the deal: To accelerate EV adoption, the government also introduced cash incentives for car owners scrapping old vehicles for electric alternatives (we covered it here).
sound_smarter: The shift from triggered to continuous curbs is the real story. Delhi has run the reactive model for years, waiting for air quality to deteriorate before acting, and it has not worked. Locking in restrictions from November regardless of the daily reading removes the political discretion that let enforcement slip in previous winters. Whether that holds when parking fees and construction bans start costing people money is the test this policy has never passed before.

title: Skyroot Aerospace prepares India's first private orbital rocket launch
text: Indian space startup Skyroot Aerospace has set a July 12 to August 4 launch window for the Vikram-1, the first attempt by an Indian private company to place a satellite in orbit. The Vikram-1 stands seven storeys tall and can carry payloads of up to 350 kilograms into low Earth orbit. Founded by former Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) engineers, Skyroot became India's first space unicorn after raising USD 60 million in May. The test flight carries a mix of domestic and international customer payloads and aims primarily to collect performance data on propulsion, guidance, and stage separation. The launch comes as India opens its space sector to private players, targeting a USD 44 billion space economy by 2033.
anchor: Skyroot Aerospace prepares India's first private orbital rocket launch

title: Blend over backwards
text:
A fuel policy the government calls a success has put motorists on the streets. Drivers protested India's mandatory 20% ethanol-blended petrol at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi on Sunday, forcing ministers, carmakers, and insurers onto the defensive.

The mandate: The blend, known as E20, has been compulsory since last year, and motorists no longer have a choice of grade at most pumps. Complaints over reduced mileage and engine wear have made it one of the biggest political flashpoints for Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government in the world's third-largest car market. Sunday's demonstration was led by Tehseen Poonawalla, a New Delhi socialite and Congress party supporter. We covered the rollout here.

The trigger: Anger intensified after Attorney General R. Venkataramani told a court hearing that E20 was an "experiment" whose results would emerge next year. The government denied the remark was made, but video of the hearing went viral. Venkataramani later clarified that he used the word in the context of ethanol supply volumes, not the policy itself.

Industry pushback: At a joint press conference on Saturday, carmakers including Maruti Suzuki, Toyota Kirloskar Motor, Hero MotoCorp, TVS, Hyundai, and Bajaj Auto defended the fuel. Maruti Suzuki said that of 28.4 million cars it serviced in the 2025-26 financial year, more than 15 million were over three years old and not E20-certified, with no reported corrosion, wear, or component damage. The company put the mileage loss at 3 to 3.5%, or roughly 0.6 km per litre on a car returning 20 km per litre, and confirmed no retrofitment kit is on the market.

The fine print: Insurers added to the confusion. After ICICI Lombard and ACKO warned that engine-damage claims on non-compatible older cars could be rejected as improper fuel use, the government pressed insurers and manufacturers to clarify that E20 alone will not void a policy. The residual exposure remains, since a specific engine claim tied to prolonged ethanol use in an incompatible vehicle can still be declined.
sound_smarter: The government's economic case rests on a lower crude-import bill, yet drivers have seen no matching fall at the pump, only thinner mileage and a fuel they cannot refuse. Owners of pre-2023 cars now carry a cost the Centre keeps describing as a benefit, and the reassurances on safety and insurance arrive with quiet caveats that leave the oldest vehicles most exposed. A policy sound on the balance sheet has become a household grievance, and that is precisely what moves votes.
anchor: A fuel policy the government calls a success

title: With a watchful eye
text:
The Centre has ordered Meta to disable all Instagram ads promoting child sexual abuse material. On Saturday, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) gave the company seven days to explain how advertisements promoting child sexual exploitative and abuse material (CSEAM) passed through its systems in the first place

The trigger: A BBC Eye investigation found around 30 Instagram ads using terms such as "rape video" and "child video," redirecting users to Telegram channels allegedly selling the material. Meta removed the ads, disabled accounts, and blocked the URLs once the findings were flagged, and said it uses AI tools to detect such content proactively while fighting bad actors among its 3.5 billion users.

The escalation: MeitY had announced on Friday that it would summon Meta over the issue. By Saturday evening, that had hardened into a formal notice with a deadline. India's child rights body, the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR), separately opened an investigation of its own the same day.

Two fronts, one company: The notice lands the same week MeitY is pressing WhatsApp over its new username feature, which the ministry says could be exploited for impersonation, phishing, and fraud. (we covered it here.)
sound_smarter: India is steadily tightening the screws on social media companies to scrub illegal content, notably introducing a strict three-hour takedown requirement earlier this February (we covered it here). The speed of this crackdown is unusual for a ministry that typically prefers a slow burn from quiet inquiry to public notice, proving just how sensitive regulators have become to public pressure over user safety.

title: Modi and Jaishankar begin overlapping foreign tours
text: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar begin overlapping foreign tours this week, spanning the Indo-Pacific and West Asia. Modi visits Indonesia from July 6 to 8 for talks with President Prabowo Subianto, his first bilateral visit since the two countries raised ties to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, then travels to Melbourne from July 8 to 10 to meet Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and address the India-Australia CEOs Forum. He closes in Auckland from 10 to July 11, the first state visit by an Indian Prime Minister to New Zealand in four decades. Jaishankar, meanwhile, tours Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait, and Oman from July 5 to 10, before launching India's campaign for a United Nations Security Council seat for 2028-29 in New York on July 13 and attending the third India-European Union Trade and Technology Council in Brussels on July 14 and 15.
anchor: Modi and Jaishankar begin overlapping foreign tours

title: India advances ties with France, Mali, and Israel
text: India and France discussed critical minerals cooperation and closer alignment within the Group of Twenty (G20) and Paris Club at the Economic and Financial Dialogue in Aix-en-Provence on Thursday, though no agreements were signed. Separately, India and Mali held their first exports forum in Bamako, where bilateral trade topped USD 326 million in the 2025-26 financial year, a 55% rise on the year before. Both sides named cotton, mining, energy, and pharmaceuticals as priority sectors, and Mali announced an investment forum for December. The India-Israel Bilateral Investment Agreement, signed in September 2025, came into force on Friday, giving investors on both sides stronger protections while preserving each government's room for public-policy regulation.
anchor: India advances ties with France, Mali, and Israel

title: Modi launches expanded regional air-connectivity scheme
text: Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched the next phase of the regional flying scheme UDAN on Friday and inaugurated a new terminal at Jodhpur Airport. The Modified UDAN Scheme, approved in March with an outlay of around USD 3.05 billion over ten years, will develop 100 aerodromes from unserved airstrips, build 200 helipads, and continue subsidy support to keep regional airlines flying (we covered it here). The scheme also promotes indigenous aircraft, including Hindustan Aeronautics Limited's Dhruv helicopter and Dornier planes, for remote operations.
anchor: Modi launches expanded regional air-connectivity scheme

title: MeITY probes Tata breach exposing Apple supply chain data
text: The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeITY) has opened an investigation into a cyberattack on Tata Electronics after stolen files allegedly exposed confidential information about Apple's unreleased iPhone 18 Pro, including supplier lists, component details, and product images (we covered it here). The breach, claimed by a ransomware group, also reportedly affected documents linked to Tesla, Qualcomm, and TSMC. Tata Electronics has hired a global cybersecurity consultant to conduct a forensic audit while Apple is working with the supplier on long-term security measures.
anchor: MeITY probes Tata breach exposing Apple supply chain data

title: India lifts emergency gas supply restrictions
text: India has withdrawn emergency restrictions on natural gas allocation after LNG shipments from the Middle East resumed following a ceasefire and the reopening of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. The curbs, introduced during the regional conflict, prioritised gas supplies for essential sectors after disruptions prompted suppliers to declare force majeure. With imports normalising, the government has restored market-based allocation, marking the latest rollback of emergency energy measures.
anchor: India lifts emergency gas supply restrictions

title: Strait shooters
text:
India will supply Indonesia with BrahMos supersonic cruise missiles and Astra air-to-air missiles. The defence package is worth around USD 630 million, signed as Prime Minister Narendra Modi began a state visit to Jakarta on Tuesday.

The deal: Indonesia becomes the third confirmed buyer of BrahMos, after the Philippines and Vietnam. Jakarta first entered the agreement to procure the missile in March. The missiles, jointly developed by India and Russia, rank among the world's fastest cruise missiles and launch from land, sea, and air. The Astra beyond-visual-range missiles integrate onto Indonesia's Russian-made Sukhoi fighter jets. Indonesia will buy in stages rather than all at once, starting with the missiles and supporting infrastructure, then adding operator training, maintenance, and technical support for long-term deployment.

Beyond weapons: The two sides exchanged 14 agreements spanning critical minerals and rare earths, steel, health, space, and telecommunications. A Steel Authority of India (SAIL) joint venture with Krakatau Steel will build a stainless-steel slab facility in Indonesia, India's Unified Payments Interface (UPI) will integrate with Indonesia's payment system, and the Indian Institute of Management (IIM) Bangalore will open its first overseas campus at the Singhasari Special Economic Zone. Bilateral trade reached USD 28.15 billion in 2024-25, making Indonesia India's second-largest trading partner within the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).

On the record: In talks with President Prabowo, Modi set out India's MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions) maritime vision, and Prabowo backed India's 2026 BRICS presidency. Modi was also conferred the Bintang Adipurna, Indonesia's highest civilian honour, for his leadership and exceptional contribution to strengthening India-Indonesia relations.
sound_smarter: Indonesia is the third country to buy BrahMos, after the Philippines and Vietnam, and the deal caps India's rise as a genuine arms exporter. The sharper logic is commercial and strategic at once. India sells deterrence across the Indo-Pacific, banks the revenue and the goodwill, and deepens ASEAN ties, all without asking Jakarta to join any bloc or naming Beijing once.
anchor: India will supply Indonesia with BrahMos supersonic cruise

title: India and Rwanda agree to expand defence partnership
text: India and Rwanda agreed to widen their defence partnership at the second Joint Defence Cooperation Committee (JDCC) meeting in New Delhi. The two sides will deepen cooperation in military training, joint exercises, medical services, and defence industries. The partnership rests on a defence cooperation memorandum signed in July 2018 during Modi's visit to Kigali.
anchor: India and Rwanda agree to expand defence partnership

title: Four states settle decades-old Narmada payment dispute
text: Four states settled a long-running dispute over the Sardar Sarovar dam at a signing in New Delhi on Monday. Maharashtra, Gujarat, Rajasthan, and Madhya Pradesh agreed a one-time settlement of pending dues tied to cost-sharing for the Narmada project, with Union Home Minister Amit Shah and the four chief ministers present. Shah credited the resolution to “double-engine” governments, the term for states where the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) governs alongside its own government at the Centre, and linked it to recent settlements including the Haryana-Rajasthan water dispute. The agreement closes decades of friction over who pays what for the dam's construction.
anchor: Four states settle decades-old Narmada payment dispute

title: Wayanad tunnel landslide leaves workers dead and missing
text: Heavy monsoon rain triggered a landslide at a tunnel construction site in Kerala's Wayanad district, killing at least two workers and leaving seven missing. Debris buried labour camps near the project, while nine people were injured. Rescue teams from the NDRF, police and fire services are continuing search operations, with heavy rainfall hampering efforts. Authorities have opened an investigation into the incident.
anchor: Wayanad tunnel landslide leaves workers dead and missing

title: Gang's all here
text:
The United States has charged Lawrence Bishnoi, the imprisoned head of the Bishnoi Gang, and his North American deputy for ordering the 2023 murder of Sikh separatist leader Hardeep Singh Nijjar in Canada. Canada listed the Bishnoi Gang as a terrorist entity last year, citing its alleged role in a wave of extortions and shootings targeting the South Asian diaspora.

The indictment: A nine-count federal indictment, returned by a grand jury on July 1 and unsealed in Los Angeles on July 7, alleges Bishnoi directed the killing from his Indian jail cell using smuggled phones and internet-calling devices. His deputy, Satinderjeet Singh, known as Goldy Brar, is named as the North American leader of the enterprise. A third lieutenant, Rohit Godara, ran the operation's European arm. Nijjar was shot outside a Sikh temple in Surrey, British Columbia, on June 18, 2023. The FBI has since offered a USD 50,000 reward for information leading to Brar's arrest.

What the charges don't say: Crucially, the indictment does not allege any Indian government role. Royal Canadian Mounted Police Deputy Commissioner Lisa Moreland has said there is no evidence tying Indian officials to the charges, and that New Delhi cooperated with the investigation. That marks a shift from September 2023, when then Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau accused Delhi in parliament of involvement in Nijjar's killing, triggering a diplomatic drawdown of expelled diplomats and suspended visas on both sides. New Delhi called the claim absurd. Washington has taken a different route with these cases: rather than public accusation, it has built courtroom cases, as it also did with the parallel plot against Sikh separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun, which we covered here.

The wider net: The Bishnoi charges sit inside a coordinated sweep, Operation Hard Ball, run jointly by law enforcement in the US, Canada, and Europe against three India-based organised crime networks: the Bishnoi, Bhagwanpuria, and Dhanda gangs. Prosecutors have charged 37 defendants in total, with 24 already arrested, 13 in the US, three in Canada, and one in Spain, alongside seven already in custody. Ten defendants remain fugitives, including Brar. Canadian police separately arrested four Indian nationals over the killing in May 2024 and have said they are probing possible ties to the Indian government.

The backdrop: Ties between Ottawa and New Delhi have thawed under Prime Minister Mark Carney, who visited India in February and opened talks on a trade deal expected to close by year's end. Days before that visit, Canada moved to revoke the citizenship of Tahawwur Rana, jailed in India over the 2008 Mumbai attacks, a goodwill gesture ahead of Carney's trip that we covered here. Some Sikh groups have criticised Carney's approach, accusing Ottawa of failing to hold India accountable or protect Sikh Canadians from transnational repression.
sound_smarter: Washington drew a careful line here. A gang boss and his lieutenants get charged with murder, extortion, and drug trafficking, but the state actor question stays neither confirmed nor closed. That gives Carney the win he needs. He gets a US prosecution that shows accountability without forcing New Delhi to answer for anything, letting the trade deal talks proceed on schedule while the unresolved question sits with the Sikh diaspora, and not at the negotiating table.

title: Banking on blindness
text:
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has renewed its push for a crypto policy leaning towards prohibition, according to documents from May and June, seeking to bar banks and financial institutions from holding, trading, or gaining exposure to crypto assets and privately issued stablecoins.

The grey zone: India has allowed crypto to exist unregulated since the Supreme Court struck down an earlier RBI-driven ban in 2018. No formal policy on virtual digital assets exists today, neither a ban nor a regulatory framework, and the market has grown regardless: India has nearly 39 million crypto traders holding roughly USD 2.1 billion in digital assets as of May.

The ask: The RBI wants contagion risk kept entirely outside the regulated financial system, walling banks off from both crypto assets and stablecoins.

Two currencies, two worries: Foreign-currency-backed stablecoins could erode India's monetary control, the RBI argues, while rupee-backed tokens threaten government seigniorage, the revenue it earns from issuing currency, and could add stress during market volatility.

The compliance gap: India's tax department says offshore exchanges, private wallets, and peer-to-peer rupee trades already obscure beneficial ownership. Fewer than a quarter of 645,000 people who transacted in crypto in the year to March 2023 reported it, despite a 30% tax on gains.

Five years, still no bill: A 2021 bill to ban private cryptocurrencies never reached Parliament, and a promised discussion paper remains delayed. The government itself is split on the way forward: in September, the finance ministry, after consulting the RBI, had backed limited regulatory clarity instead, arguing existing tax and other laws already contained the sector's risks. The RBI's latest documents mark a harder line than that, and the government has yet to say which view prevails.
sound_smarter: The RBI and the tax department are fighting different battles here. The tax department wants to catch evasion that has already moved offshore, and walling off banks does nothing to reach that money. The RBI's real goal is narrower: keeping contagion risk out of the regulated banking system, not policing who trades what abroad. Prohibition solves the RBI's problem while leaving the tax department without a solution to tackle evasion.

title: Form over fission
text:
India and Australia finalised the administrative arrangement enabling Australian uranium exports to India, activating a civil nuclear agreement that has moved almost no fuel since it was first signed more than a decade earlier in 2014.

The fifteen-year queue: Australia holds the world's largest known uranium reserves, but its export policy barred sales to countries outside the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons (NPT), of which India is not a signatory. The door opened in 2008, when the Nuclear Suppliers Group (NSG), the 48-country body governing nuclear trade, granted India a waiver. Prime Minister Julia Gillard then pushed her Labor Party to lift its ban, and among those leading the floor fight against her was the transport minister, Anthony Albanese, who told the conference that after Fukushima, "it is absurd that we should be expanding ours." Tony Abbott and Modi signed the cooperation agreement in September 2014. It entered into force in 2015, and enabling legislation passed in December 2016. Then, almost nothing. A single trial shipment arrived in 2017. The dormancy had a hard logic: Australian material can only fuel reactors under International Atomic Energy Agency safeguards, which covered under 2 GW of India's fleet as recently as 2020, and those reactors already bought cheaper fuel from other nations. Post-Fukushima prices gave Australian miners no reason to compete for the scraps. On Thursday, Albanese completed the deal he once fought.

What changed in Delhi: India now wants the fuel. The Centre's Nuclear Energy Mission targets 100 gigawatts (GW) of nuclear capacity by 2047, up from just under 9 GW today across 25 reactors supplying roughly 3% of electricity. The Sustainable Harnessing and Advancement of Nuclear Energy for Transforming India (SHANTI) Act, passed in 2025, replaced the Atomic Energy Act of 1962 and opened the sector to private and foreign investment. India’s domestic mines cover only a fraction of the uranium that build-out requires.

What changed in Canberra: Uranium is worth selling again. Spot prices briefly topped USD 100 per pound in January 2026, and long-term contract prices are at their highest since 2008, pulled up by reactor build-outs, data centre demand, and a decade of underinvestment in new mines. A joint statement on energy security placed the arrangement against supply disruption in West Asia, committing both sides to keeping coal, diesel, other liquid fuels, and natural gas moving. Australia ships liquefied natural gas (LNG) to India. India ships refined fuels back. Australia also repeated its support for India's NSG membership, which China has blocked since 2016.

Cleared for landing: At the third India-Australia Annual Summit in Melbourne, the prime ministers announced a Joint Declaration on Defence and Security Cooperation, replacing the 2009 declaration. Both militaries will expand aircraft deployments from each other's territory, run more complex exercises, and consult on Indo-Pacific developments. An Annual Defence Ministers' Dialogue was established, a Maritime Security Collaboration Roadmap agreed, and the Indian Coast Guard signed a memorandum with Australia's Maritime Border Command.

Minerals and machines: The governments agreed to the Australia-India Partnership on Cyber, Critical Technologies and Supply Chains (PACTS), replacing a 2020 framework, with workstreams on trusted vendor frameworks, undersea cable protection, semiconductor supply chains, and critical minerals recycling.

Money and mortarboards: Modi and Albanese addressed the Australia-India CEOs Forum, calling for an early conclusion of the Comprehensive Economic Cooperation Agreement (CECA). India's University Grants Commission cleared Flinders University for Bengaluru and Victoria University for Gurugram, and Australian institutions will return three Tamil Nadu antiquities. Modi will be in Australia until July 10, when he leaves for New Zealand, his first-ever visit to the nation as Prime Minister.

### The verdict

- Commercial contracts follow within the year. Governments do not finalise enabling paperwork in the abstract. With the SHANTI Act letting private players build reactors, expect the first supply agreements between Australian miners and Indian buyers before the next annual summit.
- The bilateral route has beaten the multilateral one. This arrangement delivers what NSG membership was supposed to: access to fuel. Each deal of this kind makes Beijing's veto less relevant, and India's formal membership bid matters less each year it stays blocked.
- Uranium joins the minerals conversation. India's 100 GW target cannot run on domestic mines. Expect fuel supply to surface in CECA negotiations alongside lithium and rare earths, converting Australia from commodity vendor into a pillar of Indian energy security.
- The defence declaration is the sleeper document. Reciprocal aircraft deployments put Indian maritime patrol aircraft within reach of Australia's Indian Ocean approaches, including the Cocos Islands.

title: Name your price
text:
Google is fighting to keep brand names inside the ad auction. On Tuesday, the company filed a 4,761-page appeal against a Delhi High Court ruling that found it liable for trademark infringement through its AdWords keyword system.

The trigger word: Bathroom fittings maker Hindware sued Google after rivals bought “Hindware” as a keyword, making their ads appear when consumers searched for the brand. Grohe, Cera and its website developer, Omkara settled during trial. Google fought on and lost.

Court logic: In May, Justice Mini Pushkarna ordered Google to pay around USD 31,600 (INR 3 million) in damages plus costs. The court rejected Google’s passive-intermediary defence, finding that it actively profits from the auction system and cannot wash its hands of resulting infringement.

Google’s pitch: Google says keywords are invisible, internal backend triggers, not trademark use. It argues the ruling would make India a global outlier and hurt consumer choice by limiting comparison shopping.
sound_smarter: The loudest defenders of the ruling are not regulators, but Indian tech founders like Nithin Kamath and Sridhar Vembu, which is the same crowd that usually bristles at state interference in platform markets. That irony points to the real pain that smaller Indian brands face when they have to pay Google just to keep their own name at the top of their own search results.
anchor: Google is fighting to keep brand names inside

title: Charging up the ecosystem
text:
New Delhi just slashed import duties on key electronics components and battery-making machinery until March 31, 2029.

The exemptions: The rules wipe out 5% to 7.5% tariffs on parts for wireless charging, lithium-ion cell production equipment, and automotive displays.

The Apple angle: The exemption directly covers wireless charging modules. This clears the runway for Apple’s assembly partners – like Foxconn and Tata Electronics – to build MagSafe components domestically instead of importing them at a markup. The tax holiday feeds into New Delhi’s aggressive target to scale electronics manufacturing to USD 500 billion by fiscal year 2030, of which smartphone manufacturing has risen 28-fold over the last decade.

China hedging: Apple now builds roughly a quarter of all iPhones in India, including the entire iPhone 17 Pro lineup. Lowering input costs keeps India competitive as a manufacturing alternative to China.

Powering up: By exempting 85 types of assembly machinery, the government wants to anchor the entire electric mobility and battery ecosystem domestically, rather than just importing finished packs.
sound_smarter: It is easy to dismiss minor tariff tweaks as insufficient, but this is a crucial part of a bigger strategy. By cutting duties on high-value inputs while maintaining them on finished goods, India is systematically forcing global tech giants to move beyond simple assembly and actually deepen their local supply chains.
