title: Algorithmic intervention
text:
The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) directed Meta to revamp its content moderation algorithms and submit a roadmap to curb deepfakes, propaganda, and synthetic content across its platforms on Friday.

What MeitY wants: Meta must strengthen moderation, accelerate the execution of government takedown requests, strictly adhere to data-localization rules, and re-engineer algorithms to actively throttle the reach of manipulated media.

Meta’s response: The company acknowledged technical gaps in handling child sex abuse material and deepfakes during talks with ministry officials, promising concrete technical measures ahead of follow-up meetings next week. We covered the apology from Meta here.

Regulatory pressure: The push follows recent amendments to India's IT Intermediary Rules, which tightened due-diligence requirements and increased platform accountability for AI-generated content. MeitY gave platforms a three hour window to take down deepfakes back in February (we covered it here).
sound_smarter: Throttling deepfakes at the algorithmic level protects users from viral disinformation and targeted scams before they spread, but automated filters are blunt instruments. Overly aggressive suppression systems frequently catch legitimate speech, news, and satire in the crossfire, meaning improved safety could come at the expense of automated collateral censorship for everyday users.
anchor: The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)

title: Clearing the ledger
text:
India wants its small businesses to get paid faster. On Friday, the Lok Sabha passed the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026, four days after it cleared the Rajya Sabha, overhauling the 20-year-old Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (MSMED) Act.

The clock: The amendment targets the chronic issue of delayed payment and mandates that mediation must be completed within 90 days. Buyers challenging an arbitral award already had to deposit 75 per cent of it with the court, but release of that money to the supplier was left to judicial discretion. Now, if the challenge sits pending for more than six months, courts must release at least 50 per cent of the awarded amount to the MSE supplier upfront.

The collections: To make awards enforceable, the bill lets a mediated settlement or arbitral award be recovered as an "arrear of land revenue" through the district administration. It also requires all Central Public Sector Enterprises to route their MSME payments through the Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS), an invoice-discounting platform, and nudges state governments to put their own enterprises on it too.

Decriminalisation: The bill shifts the regulatory framework from criminal to civil compliance. Previously, failing to register or supply information could result in a criminal conviction or a fine. These are now decriminalised into graded penalties: a warning for the first instance of furnishing wrong information, and financial penalties for subsequent violations.

The platform: The amendment also gives statutory permanence to the Udyam Registration Portal as a free, voluntary digital platform, and formally incorporates the twin criteria of "investment in plant/machinery" and "turnover" for MSME classification into the Act.
sound_smarter: India's courts already held 75 per cent of a disputed award in escrow, so buyers never had a genuinely free ride. The supplier's working capital depended on which court and which judge they drew, since the courts had no floor for what to release mid-dispute. That inconsistency has now been fixed.
anchor: India wants its small businesses to get paid

title: The repo men get rules
text:
India is reining in aggressive loan recovery practices across its lenders. On Thursday, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) issued new directions governing how banks, NBFCs, and recovery agents retrieve outstanding dues, explicitly expanding the definition of harassment to cover social media shaming and public intimidation. The rules take effect on January 1, 2027.

The conduct: While odd-hour calls and physical threats were already banned, the RBI has widened the net. Recovery agents can no longer post a borrower’s personal details on social media, contact or intimidate their friends, relatives, and co-workers, or make false representations about the legal consequences of defaulting.

The hardware lock: Lenders are now banned from remotely disabling a defaulting borrower’s mobile phone, tablet, or laptop to compel repayment. The only exception is if the loan was specifically taken out to purchase that exact device. Even then, banks cannot impose hardware locks all at once (ab initio). They must take a gradual approach and are strictly barred from cutting off essential baseline functions, including incoming calls, SMS, and emergency SOS features. If a borrower clears their pending dues, lenders are required to fully restore device functionality within one hour.

The backdrop: Indian household debt hit a record 45.5 per cent of GDP as of September 2025. RBI's Financial Stability Report shows that the rise is driven largely by a surge in unsecured consumer lending. Easy credit has become the engine of India's retail economy: smartphone financing alone is projected to reach 42 per cent of all sales in 2026, up from 35 per cent last year.
anchor: India is reining in aggressive loan recovery practices

title: UPI transactions will remain completely free for individual consumers and peer-to-peer users
text: The Ministry of Finance reiterated that proposed amendments to Section 10A of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act are aimed at ensuring the long-term technological sustainability, cybersecurity, and infrastructure expansion of the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) ecosystem. Under the proposed framework, everyday consumer and P2P payments will face zero transaction fees, while any future Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) will be nominal, threshold-based, and limited to a select subset of merchant transactions (we covered it here and here).
anchor: UPI transactions will remain completely free for individual consumers and peer-to-peer users

title: India surpasses 300 GW of installed non-fossil fuel electricity generation capacity
text: Non-fossil fuel sources now comprise over 54% of India’s total power capacity (~552 GW), led primarily by solar power (164.59 GW) and wind power (58.14 GW). This puts India at over 60% of its target to reach 500 GW of non-fossil energy capacity by 2030. India is expanding domestic solar modules, wafers, and ingots capacity through Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes. India already requires locally assembled solar modules in state-backed projects and domestically made solar cells become mandatory across all projects from June 2026. The requirements for ingots and wafers were announced earlier in March (we covered it here).
anchor: India surpasses 300 GW of installed non-fossil fuel electricity generation capacity

title: Judicial reset through parliamentary noise
text:
The Lok Sabha passed the Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026, by voice vote without debate on Monday as Opposition members drowned out the floor demanding answers on student protests.

Parliamentary pandemonium: Protesting MPs demanded Home Minister Amit Shah address a Delhi police crackdown on students, leaving Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal to clear the legislation through the noise.

Judicial reset: The bill repeals the Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021, which provides for appointments and terms and conditions of service for various Tribunals, after the Supreme Court struck down key provisions for violating judicial independence. It establishes a new National Tribunals Commission, headed by a retired Supreme Court judge or High Court Chief Justice, to standardize member selection, salaries, and oversight.

Government pitch: Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal described the law as part of the government's “reform express” to bring uniformity, efficiency, and transparency to specialized tribunals.
sound_smarter: By institutionalizing a central selection commission, New Delhi is finally aligning with Supreme Court mandates to shield tribunal appointments from executive influence. However, pushing structural judicial reforms through without parliamentary discussion risks inviting a fresh round of challenges.
anchor: The Lok Sabha passed the Tribunals Reforms Bill,

title: Testing the states
text:
India's examination revolt has acquired a state-level sequel. Thousands of students and unemployed young people marched on the Jharkhand legislature in Ranchi on Monday, with police using tear gas, batons and water cannons after demonstrators crossed barricades.

The grievance: The protests, organised under the JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch, concern alleged irregularities in Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC) recruitment examinations, including question-paper leaks. They began on July 25 and had entered their 17th day by Monday.

The concessions: Jharkhand's higher education minister, Sudivya Kumar Sonu, said on Sunday the state has agreed to cancel the 14th JPSC preliminary examination and the 2023-25 backlog exams, open a Criminal Investigation Department (CID) probe, seek an Enforcement Directorate (ED) investigation into alleged financial irregularities, and set up a fast-track court to file charge sheets within 90 days. Sonu said the government has met roughly 98 per cent of demands.

The holdout: Protesters reject that figure. Their central demand, a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe rather than a state-run CID one, remains unmet, as does cancellation of the JSSC Combined Graduate Level (CGL) exam. The Bharatiya Janata Party, Jharkhand's opposition, protested outside Chief Minister Hemant Soren's residence on Monday demanding the same CBI probe.

The parallel: July 25 was also the day the Cockroach Janta Party ended its month-long Delhi agitation after Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned and the Centre promised exam reform (we covered it here). The two disputes stay distinct, one over a national medical entrance exam and the central government, the other over state recruitment exams under an opposition-run state, but the underlying grievance has now crossed both institutional and party lines.
sound_smarter: Jharkhand's government is refusing a CBI probe because the CBI answers to the Centre, currently run by the same BJP now protesting outside the Chief Minister's residence. Handing the investigation to Delhi would give a Union-run agency a foothold inside a state Jharkhand Mukti Morcha governs. The bigger signal is behavioural: Gen Z has forced a ministerial resignation in Delhi and a near-capitulation in Jharkhand within the same month, regardless of which party held power. Any party chasing power in 2029 will have to treat examination integrity and youth unemployment as a liability that can materialise within weeks, well before the next ballot.
anchor: India's examination revolt has acquired a state-level sequel.

title: Air India captain undergoes confirmatory drug testing
text: Air India flight AI2379's captain is undergoing confirmatory drug testing after an initial post-flight screening flagged a result requiring further laboratory analysis, India's Civil Aviation Ministry said on Sunday. The Airbus A320, flying from Phuket to Delhi on August 4, lost roughly 300 feet of altitude during severe turbulence over Odisha before stabilising and landing safely, and both pilots have been taken off flying duty pending the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau's probe into what has been classified as a Serious Incident. Air India said the results have not been shared with the airline and it cannot comment on the findings. Earlier this week, the airline named Tewolde Gebremariam as chief executive. We covered the appointment here.
anchor: Air India captain undergoes confirmatory drug testing

title: Urban unemployment holds steady at 6.7 percent
text: India's overall Labour Force Participation Rate for persons aged 15 and above fell to 54.6 percent in the April to June quarter, down from 55.5 percent the previous quarter, according to the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation's latest Periodic Labour Force Survey bulletin, with urban unemployment holding broadly stable at 6.7 per cent. The share of regular wage or salaried employees rose in both rural areas, to 16.1 percent, and urban areas, to 49.3 percent, while rural employment in agriculture fell to 52.9 percent from 55.8 percent.
anchor: Urban unemployment holds steady at 6.7 percent

title: Bangladeshi PM presses India on "conducive environment" for ties
text: Bangladeshi Prime Minister Tarique Rahman told India's newly appointed High Commissioner to Dhaka, Dinesh Trivedi, on Monday that a "conducive environment" is needed to boost bilateral ties. Rahman renewed Dhaka's call for India to extradite former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, who has lived in India since fleeing Bangladesh in August 2024. The remarks mark the first time Rahman's government has explicitly tied warmer ties to conditions being met. Hasina has stated that she will return to Bangladesh and face trial in December (we covered it here).
anchor: Bangladeshi PM presses India on "conducive environment" for ties

title: TRAI extends anti-fraud numbering to utilities, courier sectors
text: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has directed telecom providers to begin phased rollout of 1601-series numbers for service and transactional calls made by utilities, courier and logistics companies, with onboarding to be completed within 90 days. The move extends a framework already used by banking, financial services and insurance firms to help consumers distinguish legitimate business calls from fraudsters impersonating them through ordinary 10-digit numbers. Numbers will be allocated directly to verified entities rather than intermediaries or aggregators, and cannot be used for promotional calls.
anchor: TRAI extends anti-fraud numbering to utilities, courier sectors

title: A rare offramp
text:
A US judge has closed the criminal case against Gautam Adani for good. On Monday, District Judge Nicholas Garaufis dismissed the fraud and bribery indictment against Gautam Adani, his nephew Sagar Adani, and former Adani Green CEO Vneet Jaain, after federal prosecutors moved to drop the case.

The backstory: US prosecutors said in November 2024 that Adani and seven others paid USD 250 million in bribes to Indian officials to win solar power contracts, which were expected to bring in more than USD 2 billion in profit over twenty years. Prosecutors also said Adani misled US investors by stating that the company followed strict anti-corruption standards. Investors had put more than USD 3 billion into the deals through loans and bonds.

The optics problem: Garaufis granted the Justice Department's motion to dismiss with prejudice, but pressed prosecutors on whether Adani's November 2024 pledge to invest USD 10 billion in the United States, made days after Donald Trump's re-election, factored into the decision to walk away.

In another case: In a separate resolution to civil charges brought by the US Securities and Exchange Commission over the same allegations, Gautam Adani agreed to pay USD 6 million, while his nephew, Sagar Adani, agreed to pay USD 12 million in May.
sound_smarter: With no conviction and no exoneration, the investors and compliance officers who pulled back in 2024 have no finding to point to in either direction. Adani will re-enter global capital markets with the question still open, and the cost of borrowing will tell him what the market decided.
anchor: A US judge has closed the criminal case

title: BRICS nations actively discuss options to interconnect fast payment systems and central bank digital currencies
text: Speaking ahead of the 2026 BRICS summit hosted by India, Reserve Bank of India Governor Sanjay ‌Malhotra highlighted cross-border payments as a key focus area aimed at significantly lowering transaction costs across member economies. Beyond digital currency linkages, India plans to continue advancing the internationalization of the rupee to encourage local currency usage in bilateral trade.
anchor: BRICS nations actively discuss options to interconnect fast payment systems and central bank digital currencies

title: Fitch Ratings affirmed India’s long-term sovereign credit rating at "BBB-" with a stable outlook
text: The rating agency projected India's GDP growth at 6.4% for FY27, noting that while this marks a slight moderation from the prior three-year average of 7.4%, it remains roughly triple the median for "BBB"-rated peers. Fitch emphasized that strengthening policy credibility, resilient corporate and bank balance sheets, and structural tax reforms continue to insulate the economy from external risks, such as geopolitical energy shocks. The stable outlook reflects expectations that sustained macroeconomic growth will support gradual fiscal consolidation and lower government debt metrics over time.
anchor: Fitch Ratings affirmed India’s long-term sovereign credit rating at "BBB-" with a stable outlook

title: Pause for panel
text:
The government has sent its foreign-funding bill to a committee. On Wednesday, the Lok Sabha referred the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment (FCRA) Bill to a 31-member Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) amid Opposition protests. The committee is due to submit its report in the first week of the Winter Session.

Previously: Introduced in March, the bill drew objections from Opposition parties and Christian civil society groups, who argue it will be used to target NGOs and minority-run institutions. Delegations from Kerala and Mizoram have raised their concerns directly with Home Minister Amit Shah; the government denies the bill targets any community (we covered it here).

The asset trap: Under Section 14B and Chapter IIIA, a routine delay on the FCRA Online Portal, or a minor technical lapse, can trigger automatic certificate cessation. That instantly hands a Designated Authority provisional control of an NGO's foreign contributions and assets, including those funded only partly by them. Without restored registration, control becomes permanent and the authority may transfer or sell them. Places of worship must retain their religious character.
sound_smarter: Current rules already trigger asset seizure upon license cancellation; this bill expands the net to include expired registrations. NGOs must now treat FCRA compliance as a perpetual condition of property ownership, effectively forcing them to maintain government favor just to retain legacy assets. The legislative tug-of-war will intensify.

title: Full circle, at a premium
text:
Rosneft backed Nayara Energy is now selling fuel back to Russia. A 42,000-tonne petroleum shipment from Nayara's Vadinar refinery reached Russia in early August, according to data provider Kpler.

The premium: The shipment marks the first time ever that Russia has imported fuel from India, signalling that Russia’s fuel crisis is severe enough to justify paying for supply from as far as South Asia. The cargo took a lengthy detour, moving through a ship-to-ship transfer off Egypt's Damietta port before reaching its destination.

The real exposure: Nayara and Reliance Industries account for the bulk of India’s Russian crude imports. The trade has put India among five countries named in a US bill that authorises tariffs up to 100% on buyers of Russian oil (we covered it here). Nayara has been sanctioned by the European Union (EU) since July 2025.
sound_smarter: The optics here are worse than the economics. This shipment earns India revenue rather than funding Russia's war effort, but it hands hawks in Washington a fresh headline just as it prepares to levy tariffs tied to India's actual crude purchases from Moscow.
anchor: Rosneft backed Nayara Energy is now selling fuel

title: Rights of mine
text:
The Centre is closing a mineral-tax window the Supreme Court confirmed two years ago. Coal and Mines Minister G. Kishan Reddy introduced legislation on Monday prohibiting states from taxing mineral rights and restricting levies based on a mineral's quantity, value, or royalty.

The restriction: The bill would void state taxes and cesses left unpaid or unrecovered once it takes effect. Money already collected stays with the states, drawing a line between states that converted taxing power into revenue and those with claims still pending.

The opening: In 2024, the Supreme Court ruled 8–1 that royalty is not a tax. Courts had long treated it as one, capping what states could separately charge. Removing that classification cleared the cap, letting states impose their own levies on mineral rights and mineral-bearing land. The judgment also gave Parliament a route back in, to restrict that taxation through the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, though it treated mineral-bearing land as a separate state power. The Centre lost a review attempt and filed a curative petition before turning to legislation.

The early movers: States had already begun using the ruling. Jharkhand raised its coal cess from INR 100 (USD 1.05) to INR 250 (USD 2.62) per tonne, and its iron ore cess from INR 100 to INR 400 (USD 4.19), in 2025. Karnataka projected INR 30 billion (USD 314 million) from a proposed levy in 2026–27, awaiting central approval. The bill would replace these state-level choices with conditions set by Delhi.

The cost case: Reddy argues uneven, excessive levies make mines unviable, discourage production, and raise costs for power, steel, and cement. A former mining-industry official estimates additional liabilities above INR 1.5 trillion (USD 15.7 billion), though that figure includes historical claims dating to 2005. Coal and Mines Minister G. Kishan Reddy introduced legislation on Monday prohibiting states from taxing mineral rights and restricting levies based on a mineral's quantity, value, or royalty.
sound_smarter: The bill lowers the risk of a state-by-state cost spiral for power, steel and cement, but it also transfers revenue away from the states that bear mining’s environmental and infrastructure costs. Unless Delhi replaces some of that income, cheaper minerals upstream could mean fiercer fiscal and political resistance at the mine gate.
anchor: The Centre is closing a mineral-tax window the

title: NASA invites ISRO to join Moon Base programme
text: The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) invited the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) to join its Moon Base programme, aimed at establishing a sustained human presence near the south pole of the moon. The invite was extended at the ninth meeting of the India-US Civil Space Joint Working Group at ISRO headquarters in Bengaluru on August 5 and 6. The two sides also agreed to advance talks on sharing open scientific data under the Artemis Accords, and the invitation builds on NISAR (NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar), the joint Earth observation satellite the two agencies launched in July 2025.
anchor: NASA invites ISRO to join Moon Base programme

title: India signs trade talks framework with the SACU
text: India and the Southern African Customs Union (SACU), comprising South Africa, Botswana, Namibia, Eswatini, and Lesotho, signed the Terms of Reference for negotiations towards a Preferential Trade Agreement on Wednesday. The Terms of Reference (ToR) mark India's first such framework with an African region. Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal called for a balanced and equitable agreement, citing scope for India to supply affordable medicines and IT talent to the bloc. Talks will cover eight chapters, including trade in goods, rules of origin, and a bilateral safeguard mechanism.
anchor: India signs trade talks framework with the SACU

title: Wings and wagers
text:
The Ministry of Defence has floated an INR 1 trillion (USD 10.49 billion) tender to replace its ageing Soviet-era airlifters. Issued on August 12, the Medium Transport Aircraft (MTA) programme invites Indian companies to partner with global manufacturers to build 60 transport aircraft with an 18-30 tonne cargo capacity.

The contenders: The tender has been issued to multiple companies, of which Tata Advanced Systems Limited (TASL) and Mahindra Defense have announced partnerships to advance the project. TASL has tied up with Lockheed Martin to pitch its C-130J Super Hercules, and Mahindra Defense has teamed up with Embraer, which has pitched its KC-390 Millennium aircraft to India. The rest have not yet announced partnerships.

The backdrop: The aircraft will replace the Indian Air Force's Antonov An-32 fleet, in service for three decades and involved in a fatal crash in June that killed five personnel. Selection could take more than two years given the scale of the technical and commercial evaluation. India is actively looking to sharpen the air force’s combat edge, with deals for new transport planes, airborne early warning and control (AEW&C), and 114 Rafale fighter jets.
sound_smarter: The tender might be for airlifters, but the companies are all competing to become a key anchor of India's defence aviation complex. A win here gives the company a leg-up in future defence contracts, and with India aggressively pushing fleet modernisation, it would be a frontrunner for all of them.
anchor: The Ministry of Defence has floated an INR

title: Fast and funded
text:
Tamil Nadu changed its government, not its industrial pitch. On Thursday, Chief Minister Joseph Vijay's administration signed 97 investment agreements worth INR 674.52 billion (USD 7.08 billion), projected to create more than 100,000 jobs.

Foreign interest: Overseas projects totalled INR 150.5 billion (USD 1.58 billion). Daimler pledged INR 40 billion (USD 419 million) to expand its Chennai facility, while Saint-Gobain committed INR 20 billion (USD 210 million) to a new plant in Krishnagiri and an expansion in Kanchipuram.

Not all his: This was Vijay's first investment conclave since his party ended Tamil Nadu's two-party duopoly in May. Factories take months to negotiate, and the two largest disclosed foreign deals involve companies already operating in the state, meaning much of this pipeline was in motion before he took office. Yet the money still landed on his watch, and at scale. Vijay retained Chief Secretary M. Sai Kumar through February 2027, keeping the bureaucracy that delivers on these pledges intact.
sound_smarter: Dravidian parties have traded power for decades, but none have touched the industrial playbook, because the welfare schemes that win Tamil Nadu's elections are funded by the growth these factories deliver. Vijay is not choosing continuity out of caution, as keeping the industrial policy stable is the one thing every party that has ever governed Tamil Nadu has agreed on.
anchor: Tamil Nadu changed its government, not its industrial

title: China extends anti-dumping duties on Indian optical fibre
text: China has extended anti-dumping duties on Indian single-mode optical fibre for another five years. The measures will remain in force from Friday at rates ranging between 7.4 percent and 30.6 percent depending on the exporter, with Sterlite Technologies subject to 7.4 percent and Aksh Optifibre and Finolex Cables each facing 30.6 per cent. China's Ministry of Commerce said a year-long expiry review found that removing the duties could allow dumping and harm to domestic producers to continue or recur. China first imposed the measures in 2014 and previously renewed them for five years in 2020.
anchor: China extends anti-dumping duties on Indian optical fibre

title: Prep talk
text:
India celebrated its 80th Independence Day on Saturday, and Prime Minister Modi's address from the Red Fort was explicit on what the government wants to capitalise on: its demographic dividend. India's youth have spent 2026 on the streets fighting for fair exams and more jobs, and the Red Fort was where Modi chose to answer them. He promised free online coaching for competitive examinations, training for 10 million young people in artificial intelligence within a year, and a nationwide talent hunt to groom children aged five to 15 for a 2036 Olympics he wants India to host.

After the anger: The pledges follow a year of pressure, as youth across India spent much of 2026 protesting leaked examination papers, patchy recruitment, and a shortage of secure jobs. We covered the protests that led to the resignation of the education minister here.

Already on offer: Much of what Modi announced already exists. The Self Assessment Test and Help for Entrance Exams (SATHEE) platform, run with the Indian Institute of Technology, Kanpur, provides free coaching for engineering, medical, and civil service examinations, and the AI pledge scales up the IndiaAI Mission that has run since 2024. Modi attached no budget, launch date, list of covered examinations, or training standard to either announcement.

Also from the ramparts: Modi reaffirmed his administration's standing goals: 60 million Lakhpati Didis, rural women who earn at least INR 100,000 (USD 1,050) a year through village savings groups; 100 GW of nuclear power by 2047; and more semiconductor plants. He then added a newer pledge to rebuild the civil defence network for an age when warfare can strike refineries, banks, and data centres far from any border.
sound_smarter: Every scheme Modi named helps young people compete, without an increase in the spots to compete for. The grievances that emptied campuses onto the streets this year were leaked papers and scarce vacancies, and he met them with schemes to build a stronger applicant. Much of what Modi pledged runs through programmes already in place, leaving a better-prepared queue for the same bottleneck.
anchor: India celebrated its 80th Independence Day on Saturday,

title: Counting by caste
text:
The Indian government officially greenlit caste enumeration for the Census 2027, marking the first time the metric has been included in the national headcount since independence.

The rollout: Enumeration begins August 17 in Ladakh, Jammu & Kashmir, and Himachal Pradesh. The nationwide survey follows in February 2027, utilizing a new mobile application for digital data collection.

The caste question: Question 10 introduces an open-ended format for caste and tribe self-declaration. The decision, cleared by the Cabinet Committee on Political Affairs last year, is a direct response to intense Opposition pressure, particularly after Bihar’s state-level caste survey suggested that backward communities comprise two-thirds of its population. The Opposition is pushing to ensure that each caste group’s representation in the legislature is proportional to its share of the population rather than allowing power to be concentrated among the upper castes.

New metrics: Beyond caste, the 40-question form now tracks digital literacy, parental details, bank account holdings, and Covid-19 vaccination sites. Respondents are also asked to voluntarily provide their Aadhaar, voter ID, and mobile numbers.
sound_smarter: Caste has shaped Indian politics for decades, through quotas, coalitions, and state-level parties built on it. What changes is the currency: those fights have run on estimates until now, and a national count gives every side a hard figure to organise around. That risks fracturing the BJP's broad Hindu coalition, since voters may act on caste-specific numbers rather than the party's broader appeal.
anchor: The Indian government officially greenlit caste enumeration for

title: Dogfight
text:
Reliance and Rolls-Royce have announced a partnership to build an engine for India's stealth fighter jets. The August 14 announcement is a statement of intent, with no contract signed yet.

The prize: The engine would power the Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA), India's planned fifth-generation stealth jet, with a prototype due around 2028. India builds airframes, missiles, and radar, but decades of effort to produce a high-thrust jet engine have fallen short, leaving even the current Tejas fighter reliant on engines from General Electric (GE).

Still to be won: The announcement did not disclose any money or ownership split, and states that the two companies will explore setting up a dedicated aerospace gas turbine complex to build the engine. The Centre opened the AMCA programme to private firms in 2025. Reliance’s move sets up a contest with France's Safran, which has separately proposed a joint venture with the state-run Gas Turbine Research Establishment (GTRE) to develop a higher-thrust engine for later versions of the fighter.

Already signed: On the same day, India inked INR 1,577 crore (USD 165 million) in contracts with Tata Advanced Systems and NIBE for loitering munitions, drones that hover over a battlefield before diving into a target, for the Army under its Atmanirbhar Bharat (self-reliant India) rules. The previous week saw the Ministry of Defence floating a INR 1 trillion (USD 10.49 billion) tender to replace its ageing Soviet-era airlifters, which we covered here.
sound_smarter: India's neighbourhood has hardened. Pakistan now has Saudi and Turkish backing behind it, and Modi used the Red Fort to talk up civil defence and homegrown weapons, so the pressure to build faster is real. State labs move at the speed of the bureaucracy above them, which is why the Centre is pulling Reliance, Tata, and their foreign partners into the work that was once the state's alone. The state is making a bet that private capital can close its weaknesses before the gap is used against it.
anchor: Reliance and Rolls-Royce have announced a partnership to

title: CBDT opens a foreign asset disclosure window for small taxpayers
text: The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) launched the Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers-Disclosure Scheme (FAST-DS), first announced in the 2026-27 Budget, on Sunday, with online declarations open until 31 December. The scheme targets students, young professionals, technology employees, and relocated non-resident Indians who may have failed to disclose overseas holdings.
anchor: CBDT opens a foreign asset disclosure window for small taxpayers

title: DRI dismantles syndicate that fraudulently claimed duty exemptions
text: The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has dismantled a major syndicate that evaded over INR 2,500 crore (~USD 261 million) in customs duties by mislabeling South-East Asian areca nuts as Bangladeshi-origin to fraudulently claim SAFTA duty exemptions. Through an operation across Kolkata and Visakhapatnam, the DRI arrested nine individuals, seized cash and illicit consignments, and suspended the license of a key customs broker involved in the scheme.
anchor: DRI dismantles syndicate that fraudulently claimed duty exemptions

issue_title: Don’t be (that kind of) an influencer
title: Don’t be (that kind of) an influencer
text:
Security agencies moved against a Pakistan-based terror network days before Independence Day. On August 12, forces detained 253 people across 14 states in a coordinated sweep against the Shahzad Bhatti Network (SBN). The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) says the operation was timed to pre-empt attacks around the August 15 holiday.

Who is Bhatti: SBN is named for Shahzad Bhatti, a Pakistani social-media personality who built a following under a "333" banner posting on religion, nationalism, and India-Pakistan disputes. Indian investigators allege he has links to the Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI), Pakistan's main spy agency, and to jailed Indian gangster Lawrence Bishnoi. Bhatti, who is believed to move between Pakistan and the Gulf, denies being a gangster or a mafia figure.

The method: The Maharashtra Anti-Terrorism Squad says the network works by online radicalisation, spotting young people who vent frustration online, offering inducements, then testing them with small tasks before drawing them into cells meant to create law-and-order trouble.

The haul: The MHA says seizures included improvised explosive devices (IEDs), grenades bearing Pakistan Ordnance Factory markings, pistols, and live cartridges, citing the ordnance markings as evidence of direct cross-border links. Cumulatively, the SBN now faces more than 80 First Information Reports (FIRs) and over 200 arrests. The arrests were made under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), where charges against the accused deem to be prima facie true, and bail is an exception.
sound_smarter: The threat here is the recruitment model, which is why a takedown counted in detentions can never be final. Bhatti runs the operation from outside India, radicalising disaffected youth online from beyond the reach of any raid, so each sweep clears the operatives while the recruiter keeps posting. Naming and destroying his "network" makes for a clean Independence Day headline, but the machinery that produces the next cell remains online.
anchor: Security agencies moved against a Pakistan-based terror network

issue_title: Don’t be (that kind of) an influencer
title: Lease another day
text:
India is renting eyes over the Indian Ocean. On Monday, the defence ministry signed an INR 1,943 crore (USD 203 million) contract with General Atomics to lease two MQ 9B Sea Guardian drones for the Navy. The high altitude, long endurance aircraft will provide maritime surveillance for 30 months.

Bridging the gap: India has already purchased 31 MQ 9B drones from the United States, but the first deliveries are not expected until January 2029. The lease will expire around February 2029, making it an almost precisely timed bridge to the permanent fleet.

More ocean to watch: Chinese warships, submarines and research vessels are operating across the Indian Ocean. Beijing is also mapping the seabed, collecting information that could support future submarine operations. India already monitors the region using ships, satellites and crewed aircraft, but the Sea Guardians can remain in the air for longer and provide more continuous coverage.

More to protect: New Delhi also plans to turn Great Nicobar into a major transshipment and logistics hub near the approaches to the Malacca Strait. The port is intended to draw cargo away from Colombo, Singapore and Port Klang, although it is still awaiting final Cabinet approval.
sound_smarter: This deployment shifts the Indian Ocean’s power dynamic from sporadic monitoring to persistent surveillance. As Beijing increasingly operates in the Indian Ocean, India’s ability to maintain a 24/7 presence transforms the region from a neutral maritime zone into a contested theater where grey activities, like research vessels masking military data collection, never go unnoticed.
anchor: India is renting eyes over the Indian Ocean.
